features.title:
Everything in its place.
Your browsing, undisturbed.
features.intro: From a single page to a whole browser. KoiTab gathers everyday organizing tools into one small, paper-inspired popup.

items.title: One site, one group
items.body: Gather pages from the same site into native browser tab groups. Collapse groups and keep consistent colors; in all-windows mode, related groups move into the current window.
items.detail: Pinned tabs stay where they are and are not grouped. Common multi-part and private domain suffixes receive special handling; this is not a full public suffix list.

items.title: Only identical URLs are duplicates
items.body: KoiTab compares the complete URL, including its path, query and hash. Only identical addresses are duplicates, with pinned or active pages preferred when choosing what to keep.
items.detail: For example, /article#notes and /article#comments remain distinct, as do /page and /page/.

items.title: Save first. Close second.
items.body: Choose tabs unused for 3, 7 or 30 days. KoiTab writes their links to a local collection before closing pages that still meet the conditions.
items.detail: If saving fails, the tabs stay open. Before closing, KoiTab rechecks the URL, window, access time and active state. Changed tabs are left alone.

items.title: Two windows, two purposes
items.body: In all-windows mode, the current window holds site groups, while ungrouped pages gather in another window. Groups sit on the left, loose tabs on the right.
items.detail: Current-window mode does not move tabs between windows. Pinned tabs stay put, and the current window is never emptied while the popup is running.

items.title: Fold, search, find
items.body: Groups remember your open or collapsed preference. Automatically collapse groups at 5, 8 or 12 tabs, or search by title and URL to find a page quickly.
items.detail: Search temporarily expands matching groups. Clearing the search restores their previous state.

items.title: A collection beside your bookmarks
items.body: KoiTab's collection stores archived links. Browser bookmarks are shown read-only and can be searched alongside it. Deleting a saved link does not delete a browser bookmark.
items.detail: Deleting filtered results only affects the collection entries you confirmed. Hidden entries remain untouched.

guide.title:
See the whole picture.
Then put it in order.
guide.intro: Install KoiTab, then open the koi icon in your toolbar. Three workspaces help you understand the clutter, arrange your pages and revisit saved links.

items.title: Start with Diagnosis
items.body: Choose the current window or all windows. Review duplicates, scattered pages and idle tabs. Check the organization and archive previews before running either action.

items.title: Organize with one click
items.body: KoiTab removes duplicate pages, ungroups single-tab groups, gathers related pages and reorders tabs. Wait for it to finish before starting another organizing or deletion action.

items.title: Browse the Tabs view
items.body: Browse by site, collapse headings, or search by title and address. Select an entry to jump to its tab. The close control beside a group closes that site's pages, so use it deliberately.

items.title: Archive pages you can return to later
items.body: Choose a 3-, 7- or 30-day threshold, then archive. Active and pinned pages are excluded. If nothing qualifies, KoiTab explains why.

items.title: Return through Collections
items.body: KoiTab's saved links and browser bookmarks appear in separate sections. Open a saved entry to revisit its URL. An archive is a link, not a webpage snapshot or a copy of unsent form data.

guide.tipTitle: Leave a little room for care
guide.tip: Review the preview first. Closing duplicates does not merge unsaved page content; save your work in any page you are editing.

download.title:
A small bookmark.
Ready for your browser.
download.intro: Download the full extension for free and run it in your own browser. No account or subscription required.
download.requirements: Chrome 121+ or Edge 121+. Other Chromium browsers such as Brave and Arc may work; Firefox and Safari are not supported.
download.languageNote: Both the website and extension support Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean and Latin. The extension follows your browser language by default; choose a language at the top right to save your preference.

steps.title: Download and unzip
steps.body: Download koitab-latest.zip and extract the koitab folder. Keep it in a permanent location rather than a temporary downloads folder.

steps.title: Open the extensions page
steps.body: Enter chrome://extensions in Chrome, or edge://extensions in Edge. Turn on Developer mode.

steps.title: Load the folder
steps.body: Choose Load unpacked and select the koitab folder containing manifest.json. Pin the koi icon to your browser toolbar.

download.update: Extract the new package, replace the files in the original extension folder, then reload it on the extensions page. Keep the same directory and extension ID. Do not uninstall first, as that may clear local saved links. Consider backing up your browser profile before updating.
download.storeNote: Currently distributed as a ZIP. No browser store installation link is available yet.

privacy.title:
Your browsing stays
inside your browser.
privacy.intro: The extension organizes, diagnoses and saves links locally. It does not send tab content, bookmarks or browsing history to a KoiTab service.

items.title: tabs · Read and organize tabs
items.body: Reads titles, URLs and window information for diagnosis, search, deduplication and archiving. Moves or closes tabs in response to your actions.

items.title: tabGroups · Manage groups
items.body: Creates, updates and collapses native browser tab groups to gather pages from the same site.

items.title: bookmarks · Display bookmarks read-only
items.body: Reads browser bookmarks for display and search. KoiTab's code does not write or delete browser bookmarks.

items.title: storage · Save local settings and links
items.body: Uses chrome.storage.local for preferences, settings and archived links. There is no KoiTab cloud sync service.

privacy.storage: Saved links belong to the current browser profile. Uninstalling the extension, clearing extension data or losing the profile can make them unrecoverable. Archives contain titles and URLs, not page copies or login sessions.
privacy.websiteTitle: The website is separate from the extension
privacy.website: Cloudflare Workers hosts this website. Visiting it requires the hosting provider to process connection details such as your IP address and request information, and runtime logs may be recorded. These are website requests, not browsing data uploaded by the extension. The website includes no advertising or behavioral analytics scripts.

faq.title:
A few things
worth knowing.
faq.intro: Installation, organization, saved links and compatibility. The practical details, in one place.

items.a: Chrome and Edge version 121 or later are supported. Other Chromium browsers may work; Firefox and Safari do not support this extension.

items.q: Is the extension available in five languages too?
items.a: Both the website and extension support Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean and Latin. The extension follows your browser language by default; choose a language at the top right to save your preference.

items.q: What counts as a duplicate tab?
items.a: The complete URL must match, including the path, query and hash. Different routes remain separate. Page state such as unsent form input is not compared, so save your work before organizing.

items.q: Does archiving change my browser bookmarks?
items.a: No. Archives use KoiTab's own local collection. Browser bookmarks are displayed read-only. A saved entry is a link, not an offline webpage copy.

items.q: Why was an old tab not archived?
items.a: Pinned, active or navigating tabs are excluded, as are pages that do not meet the age threshold. Tabs that change while saving are also kept. Diagnosis explains why there are no eligible pages.

items.q: How do I update without losing saved links?
items.a: Replace files in the original extension directory, then reload from the extensions page. Do not uninstall first: uninstalling may clear the extension's local storage.
There is no complete one-click undo. Browser history may help reopen closed pages, but window positions, groups and form input are not guaranteed to return. Review the diagnosis preview first.

items.q: Will my saved links sync across devices?
items.a: No. KoiTab uses the current browser's local storage and has no account or cloud sync service.

items.q: Why can I not load the extension?
items.a: Enable Developer mode and select the extracted folder that contains manifest.json. Managed browsers may prohibit manually loaded extensions; follow your administrator's settings.
